assertions.assertion: Response identifies ASP.NET Core Data Protection as the root cause of the decryption failure
assertions.rationale: It attributes the failure to ASP.NET Core Data Protection and its key ring/application discriminator, not IdentityServer.

assertions.assertion: Response explains that the default application name (content root path discriminator) changed between .NET versions
assertions.rationale: It explains the default application name is based on the content root path and that how it is computed shifted between .NET 6 and .NET 8, changing the discriminator.

assertions.assertion: Response recommends calling SetApplicationName() on AddDataProtection() with an explicit application name
assertions.rationale: It shows AddDataProtection().SetApplicationName("my-identityserver") and advises pinning it.

assertions.assertion: Response mentions ensuring old Data Protection keys are still accessible (not deleted or rotated away)
assertions.rationale: It states the fix only works if the original key ring is still available and warns against deleting or rotating those keys away.
